knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(2x+y+z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u-v,\,3u+2,\,u+2v⟩
$$

 
over the domain $D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-3\le u\le -\frac{5}{2},\,-\frac{5}{2}\le v\le -1\}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{70}.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{70}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(2x+y+z)\,{|}_{x=2u-v\,y=3u+2\,z=u+2v} \\  & =2(2u-v)+(3u+2)+(u+2v) \\  & =8u+2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(8u+2)\sqrt{70}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{70}{∬}_{D}\,(8u+2)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{70}{\int }_{-3}^{-\frac{5}{2}}(8u+2)\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{70}\cdot [4{u}^{2}+2u]_{-3}^{-\frac{5}{2}}\cdot [v]_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-1} \\  & =\sqrt{70}[((-5)+25)-((-6)+36)]\cdot [((-1))-((-\frac{5}{2}))] \\  & =\sqrt{70}\cdot (-10)\cdot \frac{3}{2} \\  & =-15\sqrt{70}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}4xy\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=u,\,y=v,\,z=6-3u-2v
$$

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le 3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,6-3u-2v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(6-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(6-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =4xy\,{|}_{x=u\,y=v\,z=6-3u-2v} \\  & =4uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 3\},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}4xy\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,4uv\sqrt{14}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{14}{∬}_{D}\,4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{14}{\int }_{0}^{1}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot [{u}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{3} \\  & =\sqrt{14}[(1)-(0)]\cdot [(9)-(0)] \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot 1\cdot 9 \\  & =9\sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

{∬}_{S}{x}^{2}-2yz\,\text{d}S,

$$

$$

$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & ={x}^{2}-2yz\,{|}_{x=u+v\,y=u\,z=v} \\  & =(u+v)^{2}-2uv \\  & ={u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-\frac{1}{2}\le u\le \frac{1}{2\},\,-\frac{5}{2}\le v\le -1},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}{x}^{2}-2yz\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}+{v}^{2})\sqrt{3}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}{∬}_{D}\,{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-1}({\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-1}{[\frac{{u}^{3}}{3}+u{v}^{2}]}_{u=-1}^{u=1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-1}[(\frac{v^{2}}{2}+\frac{1}{24})-((-\frac{v^{2}}{2})+(-\frac{1}{24}))]\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-1}\frac{1}{12}+{v}^{2}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{[\frac{1}{12}v+\frac{1}{3}{v}^{3}]}_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}[((-\frac{1}{12})+(-\frac{1}{3}))-((-\frac{5}{24})+(-\frac{125}{24}))] \\  & =\sqrt{3}(-\frac{1}{12}-\frac{1}{3})-\sqrt{3}(-\frac{5}{24}-\frac{125}{24}) \\  & =5\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
